key_responsibilities: Develop and maintain embedded software for bare-metal and RTOS-based systems
Implement and test digital communication protocols (SPI, I2C, UART, CAN)
Contribute to state machines and command/control software for autonomous vehicle systems

strengths: Bare-metal firmware: STM32 Temperature Monitor 'programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1)', 'timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver', 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz.
RTOS work: Object Tracking Turret 'used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination', interrupt-driven UART commands, multi-servo PWM.
State machines and interrupts: Robocon 'interrupt-driven quadrature decoding... a 4-bit A/B transition state machine' and a 'fail-safe state machine halting all motors on controller disconnect'.
Protocols and debug tooling: UART/I2C/SPI across projects, plus oscilloscopes, logic analyzers and spectrum analyzers in the skills list.
Control and motion: closed-loop heading correction and 15 kHz PWM drive for a holonomic robot (the JD's 'motion control').
real_gaps: Rust: none in the profile; the JD calls it the primary language but frames it as 'willingness to learn'.
CAN bus: no CAN bus work anywhere in the profile (UART/I2C/SPI only).
Hardware test stands and automated unit/integration tests for embedded code: COFFIN trial runs (10/10) are manual validation, not a test-stand framework.
overstated_by_keywords: 'real-time' counted as HAVE: the evidence is deterministic timer-driven loops and FreeRTOS tasks, not formally analysed real-time behavior.
understated_by_keywords: Robocon's fail-safe state machine and interrupt-driven decoder are direct hits on 'state machines, interrupts, memory-conscious' that the keyword list scored as generic C/embedded.
screening_gaps: No Rust experience (primary language of the role)
No embedded test-stand / automated hardware-in-the-loop testing experience
llm_analysis.reasoning: This is an early-career embedded role and the profile maps almost one-to-one: bare-metal STM32 with interrupts and ADC/I2C, FreeRTOS, UART/I2C/SPI, state machines, closed-loop control and bench instruments. The real gaps are Rust and CAN, and the JD itself says it will teach Rust.
